walkthroughs.body_html:
Homes lose heat through walls, roof, floor and windows.

Loft insulation traps air to reduce conduction and convection upwards.

Cavity walls + foam slow conduction outwards.

Double glazing: two panes of glass with gas in between - much better than single.

Less heat lost = lower bills + smaller carbon footprint!

When materials heat up, their particles vibrate more and need more space.

Solids, liquids and gases all expand when heated.

Engineers leave expansion gaps in bridges and railway tracks so they don't buckle in summer.

Thermometers use expansion of mercury or alcohol to show temperature.

Energy use is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).

An electric bill charges per kWh used (often ~30p in the UK).

Better insulation, LEDs, A-rated appliances, and switching things off at the wall all reduce kWh used.

That's good for your wallet and the planet.

mcqs.q: Why do bridges have expansion gaps?
options: To save money
So they don't buckle in summer heat
To let water through
For decoration

mcqs.q: Double glazing reduces heat loss by.
options: Using a vacuum only
Trapping gas between two panes
Cooling the room down
Reflecting light only

mcqs.q: If the distance between two masses doubles, what happens to the gravitational force between them?
options: It halves — gravitational force is inversely proportional to distance.
It quarters — gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the activity of a source and the dose received by a person?
options: Activity (Bq) is the rate of nuclear decays in the source; dose (Sv) measures the biological effect of absorbed radiation on tissue.
Activity and dose are the same — both measure how dangerous the radiation is.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.
Activity is for nuclear power stations and dose is for medical X-rays.
